GOOD MORNING, HAPPY THANKFUL THURSDAY IN THE FIGHTIN’ FIFTH![image][image]Today, I’m thankful for the brave men and women in law enforcement who put their lives on the line every day to protect others.[image][image]Yesterday, at our beautiful People’s House in Boston, 18 police officers were honored with the 2026 Trooper George L. Hanna Memorial Awards for Extraordinary Bravery, the Commonwealth’s highest law enforcement honor.[image][image]These awards honor the memory of Massachusetts State Police Trooper George L. Hanna, who was killed in the line of duty in 1983. His family was there yesterday, as they are every year, to help keep his memory and legacy alive.[image][image]I also want to thank Governor Healey and her office, Public Safety Commissioner Kwan, and the Executive Office of Public Safety for recognizing these heroes and helping keep Trooper Hanna’s memory and legacy alive. These awards are an important reminder of the courage, sacrifice, and service of the men and women who protect us every day.[image][image]As a former police officer, the father of a police officer, and the father-in-law of a police officer, this is very personal to me. I know the sacrifices our law enforcement families make and the courage it takes to wear the badge.[image][image]Today, and every day, I’m thankful for the brave men, women, and canines in law enforcement here in Massachusetts and across our great nation.[image][image]CONGRATULATIONS to all 18 recipients. Thank you for your courage, your service, and for answering the call when others need you most![image][image]2026 TROOPER GEORGE L. WHAT A DAY AT MMA![image]Marinakis Hall Dedication Day[image][image]I was so proud to be at our very own Massachusetts Maritime Academy today for the dedication of the beautiful new Marinakis Hall, a building where cadets will train, learn, and prepare to lead for generations to come.[image][image]I was honored to provide a few remarks about how special this school is, its incredible history, and the deep connection between Greece and America. I even had the opportunity to speak briefly about my son, Nicholas, and remind everyone that life is precious.[image][image]What a beautiful day celebrating an incredible $5 million donation from the Marinakis family, who traveled all the way from Greece with three van loads of family and friends to be here for this special occasion.[image][image]As a proud Greek American and state representative of the Great Fightin’ Fifth, this day meant so much to me. The Greek American tradition of service, sacrifice, fighting for what we believe in, and giving back is something I hold close to my heart. We must never forget the price of freedom and the sacrifices made by so many that allow us to gather, learn, and build a better future.[image][image]One of my special moments today was pinning Chairman Evangelos Marinakis with a pin featuring the Commonwealth of Massachusetts flag and the American flag, the same special pin we proudly wear in the People’s House. Now he will wear it on his journey back to Greece, a small token of our appreciation and a lasting connection between our Commonwealth and his family.[image][image]Thank you to the Marinakis family, Admiral Francis X. McDonald, and the entire Massachusetts Maritime Academy team for making this day possible.[image][image]We are so fortunate to have this world-renowned institution right here in our district and in the Commonwealth.[image][image]WAY TO GO, MMA!
